miri.command: cargo miri test -p nros-core --lib && cargo miri test -p nros-types --lib
miri.evidence: Pass 30 (2026-08-24): cause DECODED by retrieving the actual GitHub Actions job log of safety-gate in run 32707535971 (head 083e3ed9). The log shows: nightly-2026 toolchain installed, Miri component installed, `cargo miri setup` produced a sysroot, nros-core COMPILED under Miri, and the libtest suite began executing - every test ahead of `test_zero_copy_pubsub_guard_api` passed, including the unsafe ring tests (abandoned reservation, panic-in-drop double-drop regression, capacity 1, channel ownership, double-init/double-reserve prevention, destruction, read guard lifetime, full ring, SPSC ordering, string type, wraparound). The suite then stopped with `unsupported operation: clock_gettime with REALTIME clocks not available when isolation is enabled` at SystemTime::now() <- nros_types::WallTimestamp::now() (nros-types/src/lib.rs:21) called from nros-core/src/lib.rs test_zero_copy_pubsub_guard_api line ~767. 'Miri on nros-types' was skipped only because the nros-core step exited non-zero first. This is a TEST-ENVIRONMENT blocker, not observed unsafe-code UB: no Miri UB diagnostic has ever been emitted against nros-core.
miri.classification: BLOCKED_TEST_ENVIRONMENT means Miri executed and compiled the target, then the suite could not proceed past a host-syscall dependency in one test. It is deliberately distinct from PASSED (all tests executed green) and from FAILED_CODE (a UB report against NROS code). Neither of those has been observed yet.
miri.remediation: F30-01 (Pass 30): removed the incidental wall-clock dependency - test_zero_copy_pubsub_guard_api now uses a fixed `Timestamp { sec: 1, nanosec: 0 }`, and nros-types' inherently wall-clock-bound test_wall_timestamp_now is marked #[cfg_attr(miri, ignore)] (skipped under Miri only; still runs natively). test_monotonic_elapsed needs no marker: monotonic clocks and sleep are supported under Miri isolation. Isolation is intentionally left ENABLED - the fix removes the dependency rather than weakening Miri with -Zmiri-disable-isolation.
miri.note: The decoded cause CONFIRMS Pass 29's reasoning about docs/audit/F-25-ci-miri-toolchain.patch: Miri installed and executed fine, so the toolchain was never the problem; F-25 and the F-29 diagnostics patch are now moot for this failure. nros-types' Miri step will additionally exercise (and is expected to pass) its remaining 3 tests.
miri.next_step: Re-execute the safety-gate job with F30-01 in place; only a green execution of BOTH `cargo miri test -p nros-core --lib` and `-p nros-types --lib` may transition this gate to PASS (per CLAIM-MIRI-001: configuration or installation never establishes execution or pass). Then loom remains the outstanding concurrency-verification milestone.
miri.partial_substitute: F29-12: all 8 unit-test suites (54 tests) were rebuilt from mrustc's generated C with -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all and run clean - zero sanitizer reports, so no heap-buffer-overflow, use-after-free, double-free or UBSan diagnostic in nros-core's unsafe ring code. LeakSanitizer's 1877 bytes at exit were attributed away from NROS: a no-unsafe control binary leaks 317 bytes of the same kind, 0 leak frames have a symbol naming RingBuffer, the deepest recurring frame is std::thread::Thread::new and the only test in any leak stack is the thread-spawning test_spsc_ordering. Repeatable via tools/offline-mrustc/probes/sanitizer.sh. THIS IS NOT A MIRI SUBSTITUTE: it cannot detect uninitialized reads (MemorySanitizer, impractical here) nor Rust-specific UB such as invalid &mut aliasing or invalid enum discriminants.

benchmark.evidence: F29-09: the bench binary HUNG - 2/12 runs at 2000 iterations and 1/3 at 100000 timed out - because the consumer's exit condition (local_latencies.len() >= iterations) became permanently unreachable when a receive found the shared instant queue empty; the producer committed before enqueuing. This is why the CI 'benchmarks' job had never reached a completed state (continue-on-error does not bound a hang). Fixed both halves; 20/20 and 5/5 completions afterwards with messages_sent == messages_received == 100000, and CI run 32707535971 completed the job and uploaded its artifact for the first time.
benchmark.claim_disposition: The published '6.2 us mean / 780K msg/s' and '46x faster than ROS2' are NOT supported by any executed measurement in this repository. benchmarks/results.json declares itself a TEMPLATE carrying unverified numbers. EVIDENCE_REGISTRY.md had already ordered the downgrade; Pass 29 applied it to README.md and COMPARISON.md. Cross-thread figures are scheduler-bound (2 shared unpinned vCPU) and do not characterise the ring; the same-thread figure does, and it reproduces across sessions (110.90 vs Pass 27's 112 ns/op).

overall_verdict: Substantially improved and now evidenced rather than asserted. On this branch 7 of 9 CI jobs are green against 4 of 9 on the base commit: fmt, check, test, clippy, nros-init golden, provenance and benchmarks all pass on the real toolchain. Two defects that produced false confidence were found and fixed: the test suite was nondeterministic because TcpTransport::receive discarded complete frames on peer EOF (F29-01), and the benchmark binary hung intermittently so its CI job never completed (F29-09). The published performance claims were downgraded to match the executed evidence (F29-10), which is what EVIDENCE_REGISTRY.md had already required. Two gates remain red and both are blocked by permissions rather than by unknowns in the data: the representation gate needs docs/audit/F-20-ci-fetch-depth.patch applied by someone with the `workflows` scope (the snapshot data is provably correct and the gate passes locally), and the Miri gate's cause cannot be decoded without job logs - docs/audit/F-29-ci-miri-diagnostics.patch settles it in one run. Until Miri is green, no soundness claim about nros-core's unsafe code should be treated as fully verified: Miri is the only UB detector wired into this CI and neither Miri nor loom has ever produced a passing result here. Pass 29 narrowed that gap rather than closing it - all 54 tests run clean under ASan+UBSan (F29-12, tools/offline-mrustc/probes/sanitizer.sh), which rules out heap corruption and the common UBSan classes but cannot see uninitialized reads or Rust-specific UB such as invalid &mut aliasing.
